newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reith says ACTU can't escalate coal dispute.
newsitem.headline: Reith says ACTU can't escalate coal dispute.

text.p: Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Friday the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU), Australia's top workers' body, had no power to escalate a costly Hunter Valley coal dispute.
"The fact is the ACTU has no capacity to escalate this dispute," Reith said.

"They are unable to do so because, as of the first of January (1997), the only avenue available for the coal industry to boost its prospects in the future is the strategy embodied in the government's Workplace Relations Act."
The Workplace Relations Act more clearly defines the penalties and fines which unions face if they attempt to illegally involve other unions in a dispute, a government spokeman said.
He said that, under the previous Labor Government's legislation, it was easy to call out other unions in support of strike action.
"But now unions have to think hard about their actions," the spokesman said.
Workers at Coal and Allied's Hunter Valley Number One mine have been on strike for the past four weeks.

Attempts by the company to use non-union labour to load a coal train and bypass a union picket line have remained stalled in a strike the company estimates is costing it about A$1 million in lost revenue each strike day.
Coal & Allied is 71 percent owned by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
The company's attempt to negotiate more flexible enterprise bargains, the key reason for the strike, is seen as a key battle in the industry's drive to improve profitability.
Reith has previously backed Coal and Allied's attempt to improve productivity.
"The coal industry in Australia could have a bright future and there could be a role for responsible unionism in that future," Reith said.

"They (the unions) are going to have to realise that the world has changed and the market is very difficult for the coal companies and we are going to have to change the work practices in that industry to keep it going," he said.
ACTU leaders met transport and mining union representatives on Friday to discuss the strike.
